narrative: Material PL1__MA783317 exhibits lumpy demand (CV=0.61) with ~75% active working days and a statistically significant declining trend since mid-2025. Lead times are unstable with a bimodal distribution (~1 day vs ~3 days, CV=0.56), likely reflecting two supply modes. The current SAP safety stock of 208 units is insufficient to achieve the 95% service level; the data-driven optimized safety stock of 572 units corrects this. Storage capacity (3,718 units) is binding and caps the order quantity below the unconstrained EOQ.
warnings: Storage capacity is fully consumed: safety_stock (572) + order_quantity (3146) = 3718 = max_storage_units. No buffer headroom.
Declining demand trend detected (p<0.001). Current policy parameters should be reviewed in 6 months.
Bimodal lead time distribution detected — two supply modes observed. Investigate root cause.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Lumpy but moderately frequent demand (75% non-zero days) and unstable lead times make a continuous-review (r,Q) policy preferable to periodic review. The reorder point absorbs lead-time and demand variability, while a fixed EOQ-derived order quantity minimises total ordering and holding costs. MOQ=27 is non-binding given the scale of demand.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 3,718 units is fully consumed by safety_stock + order_quantity. Any demand surge requiring a larger order cannot be accommodated without a capacity increase. This directly constrains the achievable service level upside.
